title: High Resolution Intact Proteoform Mass Spectrometry Imaging using UHMR HF Orbitrap
author: Kevin J Zemaitis

steps.title: Prepare fresh CsI calibration solution
steps.instruction: Make a 2 mg/mL cesium iodide (CsI) solution in 50 % aqueous isopropanol; use immediately for calibration and syringe priming.

steps.title: Clean HESI probe and ITT
steps.instruction: Remove the heated electrospray ionization (HESI) probe and ion transfer tube (ITT). Continuously flush the HESI probe with an Agilent 1200 series pump. Sonicate the ITT in 10–25 % formic acid in methanol, then rinse the ITT several times with HPLC‑grade nanopure water followed by methanol.

steps.title: Load sample into MALDI source
steps.instruction: Place the prepared tissue sample onto the MALDI target, close the beam valve, vent the source, then start the MALDI source roughing pump. Open the beam valve and regulate the fore‑vacuum pump to the pressure regime specified in the methods.

steps.title: Load preset methods and adjust source
steps.instruction: Load the preset instrument methods for electrospray operation onto the MALDI source. Manually set the source pressure to 7–9 Torr, adjust in‑source trapping (IST) parameters, and test HCD collision voltages.

steps.title: Load MALDI imaging method and inspect RF
steps.instruction: Load the optimized MALDI imaging method for the specific tissue type and mass range onto the UHMR Q Exactive HF. Inspect the frequency of the RF heads that drive the dual ion funnels for any deviations.

steps.title: Prime syringe with CsI and generate clusters
steps.instruction: Load the syringe and sample line with the 2 mg/mL CsI solution, prime the line, and run at 5 µL/min for several minutes until a stable ion cluster rate is observed.

steps.title: Test laser energy and crater formation
steps.instruction: Select a test measurement region (matrix only or matrix on tissue) and monitor laser energy. Visually inspect the desorption crater formed in the matrix by microscopy.

steps.title: Set laser focus for desired resolution
steps.instruction: Adjust the laser to achieve the required beam size: ≤20 µm × 20 µm for 20 µm spatial resolution, ~30 µm for broad proteoform profiling, or ~12 µm for near‑cellular resolution. Verify focus/defocus manually for each matrix and sample, and confirm crater size with bright‑field microscopy if focus is changed.

steps.title: Confirm laser fluence and define region
steps.instruction: Ensure laser fluence yields signal levels comparable to serial sections or prior analyses. Select the measurement region, including off‑tissue areas to monitor proteoform leakage and delocalization.

steps.title: Perform mass calibration and evaluate accuracy
steps.instruction: With stable clusters, select calibration peaks based on the targeted mass range using the default list (m/z 912.3346, 1691.7643, 2471.1941, 3510.4337, 4549.6734, 5588.9130, 6628.1526, 7407.5824, 8706.6319, 11304.7310) expanded up to m/z 16241.1193. Evaluate the calibration; accept it only if the RMS error is < 2 ppm with no outliers, following manufacturer recommendations.

steps.title: Check phase, line shape, and quadrupole
steps.instruction: Assess instrument phase and peak line shape across the mass range. Evaluate quadrupole isolation settings and perform any additional calibration as recommended by the manufacturer.

steps.title: Acquire MALDI‑MSI data
steps.instruction: Run the imaging acquisition using the configured parameters and maintain source pressure stability throughout the run.

steps.title: Post‑run microscopy and histological staining
steps.instruction: After imaging, remove the sample and perform high‑resolution microscopy with and without matrix. Stain the tissue (e.g., periodic acid‑Schiff for kidney, hematoxylin‑eosin for pancreas) following the cited protocols.

steps.title: Adjust laser current if focus unchanged
steps.instruction: If the beam focus was not altered during setup, adjust only the laser diode current to maintain the previously calculated fluence and record the change in the metadata.

steps.title: Perform post‑acquisition QC
steps.instruction: Inspect signal intensity, dynamic range, and proteoform fingerprint consistency pixel‑by‑pixel. Verify no delocalization or tissue‑integrity issues; datasets failing these criteria must not be submitted to HuBMAP.

steps.title: Process data and submit
steps.instruction: Run the semi‑automated data‑processing pipeline, then disseminate and submit the final dataset to the ingestion pipelines.

steps.title: Monitor vacuum pressure throughout run
steps.instruction: Continuously ensure MALDI source voltages are pressure‑regulated and that vacuum pressure does not drift, especially when using maximum extraction voltages.
